title: Counting coordinates with positive-degree influence
statement: Let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty set with probability measure $\pi$, and let $\{\phi_a:a\in\iota\}$ be a finite orthonormal basis of real functions on $\Omega$ in the $\pi$-weighted inner product, with a constant-one basis vector indexed by $0$. For $f:\Omega^n\to\mathbb R$, suppose its variance under the product measure $\pi^n$ is at most $1$. Define the stable influence at parameter $0$ of coordinate $i$ as the sum of $0^{|\{j:a_j\ne0\}|-1}\widehat f(a)^2$ over product Fourier indices with $a_i\ne0$, with the exponent interpreted as natural-number subtraction. If $0<\varepsilon\le1$, then the number of coordinates whose stable influence at parameter $0$ is at least $\varepsilon$ is at most $1/\varepsilon$.
